full_judgment: 7. The principle relating to specific reliefs are contained in the Specific Relief Act, 1877. The explanation to section 12 of the Specific Relief Act raises a presumption that the breach of a contract to transfer movable property can be adequately relieved by compensation unless and until the contrary is proved. Section 58 of the Sale of Goods Act is the only section which gives relief for breach of contract to deliver specific or ascertained goods but that section is subject : to the provisions of Chapter II of the Specific Relief Act. This section mentions that the decree may be unconditional or upon such terms and conditions as to damages, payment of the price or otherwise but they are controlled by Chapter II of the' Specific Relief Act. That Chapter is divided into six paragraphs. Paragraph (a) deals with contract which may be specifically enforced. Sections 12 to 20 belong to this category. Paragraph (b) deals with the contract which cannot be specifically enforced (Section 21). Paragraph (c) deals with the discretion of the Court (Section 22), paragraph (d) for whom contracts may be specifically enforced (Section 23), paragraph (e) contracts cannot be specifically enforced (Sections 24- 25) and (f) contracts cannot be specifically enforced except with a variation (Section 26), paragraph (g) against whom contracts may be specifically enforced (Sections 27 and 27) (a), paragraph (h) against whom contracts cannot be specifically enforced (Section 23), paragraph (i) the effects of dismissing a suit for specific performance (Section 2 ), paragraph (j) awards and directions to execute settlements (Section 30).
